_about: Doctrine index. Topics are editorial entry points: their Catechism ranges and passage lists are SUGGESTED topical connections (labelled as such in the app), distinct from the verse-level citations in ccc-links.json. Summaries are written for this app, in neutral language, and are not magisterial texts. Official documents link to the Vatican website; their text is not reproduced.

levels.doctrine: Defined / solemn teaching (e.g. conciliar dogmatic constitutions, defined dogmas).
levels.magisterial: Authoritative Church teaching that is not itself a solemn definition (encyclicals, apostolic exhortations).
levels.father: Church Father or early Christian writer: witnesses to Tradition; individual interpretations are not binding.
levels.saint: Saint, Doctor or spiritual master: spiritual authority, not doctrinal definition.
levels.reflection: Private spiritual reflection, preaching or apologetics.
levels.historical: Historical commentary; may contain interpretations that are disputed or superseded.

topics.title: The Eucharist
topics.summary: The Church teaches that in the Eucharist the bread and wine become, by the power of Christ's word and the Holy Spirit, his Body and Blood, and that the Mass makes present his one sacrifice. The Bread of Life discourse (John 6), the institution narratives and Paul's teaching in 1 Corinthians are the central passages.

topics.title: The Holy Trinity
topics.summary: One God in three Persons — Father, Son and Holy Spirit. The doctrine is drawn from the whole of Scripture and defined by the early councils; key passages include the baptismal formula, the prologue of John, and Paul's greeting in 2 Corinthians.

topics.title: Salvation
topics.summary: God's saving plan accomplished in Christ: forgiveness of sins, adoption as children of God, and the hope of eternal life. Catholic teaching holds that salvation is entirely God's gift in Christ, received in faith and bearing fruit in love.

topics.title: Grace
topics.summary: Grace is God's free and undeserved help, the gift of participating in his divine life. It is the root of justification, of faith, and of the whole life of holiness.

topics.title: Mary, Mother of God
topics.summary: Catholic teaching on Mary — Mother of God (Theotokos), ever-virgin, and model of discipleship — rests on the infancy narratives, Cana, the cross, and the woman of Revelation 12 read in the Church's tradition. Doctrinal statements are distinguished from devotional practice.

topics.title: The Communion of Saints
topics.summary: The Church is a communion of all the faithful — on earth, in purification and in heaven — who share in holy things and pray for one another. The letter to the Hebrews' 'cloud of witnesses' and Revelation's scenes of heavenly worship are frequently cited.

topics.title: Prayer
topics.summary: Prayer is the raising of mind and heart to God. The Church's teaching draws on the Psalms, the example and teaching of Jesus (especially the Our Father) and the witness of the saints; Christian prayer is always a response to God who speaks first.

topics.title: Confession and Reconciliation
topics.summary: The sacrament of Penance, in which sins committed after baptism are forgiven through the ministry of the Church. The Church points to Christ's commission on Easter evening and to the parable of the Prodigal Son as the heart of the teaching.

topics.title: Suffering and the Anointing of the Sick
topics.summary: Scripture neither explains away suffering nor leaves the sufferer alone: Job and the Psalms give voice to lament, the Servant of Isaiah 53 and the Passion of Christ give it meaning, and the Church anoints the sick.

topics.title: The Resurrection
topics.summary: Christ's Resurrection is the foundation of Christian faith, and the pledge of the resurrection of the body promised to all the faithful.

topics.title: The Moral Life
topics.summary: Life in Christ: the commandments, the Beatitudes and the law of love. Catholic moral teaching treats conscience, the virtues, grace and the gift of the Spirit together, with the Decalogue and the Sermon on the Mount as touchstones.

topics.title: Sacred Scripture and Tradition
topics.summary: Scripture is inspired by God and, together with Sacred Tradition, forms a single deposit of the Word of God entrusted to the Church. The Church teaches that Scripture is to be read in the light of the whole, in the living Tradition of the Church and the analogy of faith.

topics.title: The Church
topics.summary: The Church is the people of God, the Body of Christ and the temple of the Spirit, one, holy, catholic and apostolic. The Petrine texts and Paul's image of the body are central.

topics.title: Baptism
topics.summary: Baptism is the sacrament of new birth in water and the Spirit, incorporating the person into Christ and his Church and forgiving original and personal sin.

topics.title: The Holy Spirit
topics.summary: The third Person of the Trinity, the 'Lord and giver of life,' who spoke through the prophets, descended at Pentecost, and dwells in the Church and in believers.

topics.title: Creation
topics.summary: God freely created the world and all that is in it, and made man and woman in his image. The Church reads the creation accounts as teaching truths of faith (not as a scientific treatise).

topics.title: Marriage
topics.summary: Marriage is a covenant of the whole of life between a man and a woman, ordered to their good and to the procreation and education of children, and for baptized persons a sacrament.

topics.title: Sacrifice and Covenant
topics.summary: The covenants with Noah, Abraham, Moses and David, and the sacrifices of the Old Testament, which the Church reads as fulfilled in the new and eternal covenant in Christ's blood.

topics.title: The Incarnation
topics.summary: The Church teaches that the eternal Son of God became man, true God and true man in one Person, to save us, to show us the Father’s love, to be our model of holiness and to make us sharers in the divine nature. John’s prologue, Philippians 2 and Hebrews are the central passages.

topics.title: Original sin and the Fall
topics.summary: The Church teaches that our first parents sinned and so lost the original holiness and justice they were meant to hand on; as a result every human being is born wounded and in need of redemption, though human nature remains good. Genesis 3 and Romans 5 are the central passages.

topics.title: Grace and justification
topics.summary: The Church teaches that we are justified, made right with God, by the free gift of grace through faith in Christ, not by our own works; and that grace truly heals and transforms us so that we can cooperate with God and grow in holiness. Romans, Galatians, Ephesians and James are read together.

topics.title: The seven sacraments
topics.summary: The Church teaches that Christ instituted seven sacraments, efficacious signs of grace: Baptism, Confirmation, Eucharist, Penance, Anointing of the Sick, Holy Orders and Matrimony. They give the grace they signify when celebrated rightly.

topics.title: Holy Orders and the priesthood
topics.summary: The Church teaches that Christ’s own priesthood is shared in two ways, by all the baptized and by the ordained, who act in his person. Holy Orders has three degrees: bishop, priest and deacon. Hebrews and the pastoral letters are central.

topics.title: Anointing of the Sick
topics.summary: The Church teaches that in the Anointing of the Sick a priest anoints those who are seriously ill or growing frail, so that Christ may strengthen, comfort and, if God wills, heal them, and forgive their sins. James 5 and the healing ministry of Jesus are the basis.

topics.title: Death, judgment, heaven and hell
topics.summary: The Church teaches that each person is judged at death, that Christ will come again to judge the living and the dead, that the dead will rise, and that those who die in God’s friendship will see him face to face. Hell is the state of definitive self-exclusion from God; the Church has never said that any particular person is there.

topics.title: Purgatory and prayer for the dead
topics.summary: The Church teaches that those who die in God’s grace but still imperfectly purified undergo a purification so as to enter the joy of heaven, and that the living can help them by prayer, almsgiving, indulgences and above all the Mass. It rests on the ancient practice of praying for the dead.

topics.title: Catholic social teaching
topics.summary: The Church teaches that every person has inherent dignity, that the goods of the earth are meant for all, that society should serve the common good, and that those with power have special duties to the poor. It rests on the prophets, the Gospels and the Fathers, and has been developed in papal encyclicals since 1891.

topics.title: The dignity and sanctity of human life
topics.summary: The Church teaches that every human life, from conception to natural death, is a gift of God and has inviolable dignity because each person is made in his image. It forbids direct abortion and euthanasia, and calls for care of the vulnerable, the sick and the dying.

topics.title: Faith and reason
topics.summary: The Church teaches that faith and reason are two wings by which the human spirit rises to truth: reason can know that God exists, and faith goes further, to what God has revealed. Real science and real faith cannot contradict each other, because the same God is the author of both.

topics.title: The liturgy and worship
topics.summary: The Church teaches that the liturgy is the public worship of the whole Body of Christ, head and members, and the summit and source of the Christian life. It is celebrated through the seven sacraments, the Liturgy of the Hours and the Church’s year.

topics.title: Christian unity and the Church
topics.summary: The Church teaches that Christ prayed for his followers to be one and that the Catholic Church is where the Church of Christ subsists in its fullness, while recognizing real elements of truth and holiness in other Christian communities. Catholics are called to pray and work for unity.

topics.title: Angels
topics.summary: The Church teaches that angels are real, created, spiritual beings who serve and worship God and are sent to guard and guide us. Each person has a guardian angel. Scripture shows them at the great moments of salvation.

topics.title: Mission and evangelization
topics.summary: The Church teaches that the whole Church is missionary: every baptized person is sent to share the Good News by word and by the witness of a holy life. The Great Commission is the root of the Church’s mission.

topics.title: Virtue and the moral life
topics.summary: The Church teaches that virtues are habits of the good, built by repeated good acts and strengthened by grace. The human virtues are prudence, justice, fortitude and temperance; the theological virtues are faith, hope and charity, given by God.

topics.title: The Lord’s Day and Sunday Mass
topics.summary: The Church teaches that Sunday, the day of the Resurrection, is the Lord’s Day, on which Catholics take part in Mass and rest from unnecessary work. The third commandment honors both the Sabbath of creation and the new creation in Christ.

topics.title: Sin and mercy
topics.summary: The Church teaches that sin is an offense against God and a wound to ourselves and to the Church; it can be mortal or venial; and that where sin abounds, grace abounds all the more. God’s mercy is greater than any sin, and is received in Baptism and the sacrament of Penance.

topics.title: The Pope and the bishops
topics.summary: The Church teaches that Christ built his Church on Peter, and that Peter’s successor, the bishop of Rome, is the visible head of the whole Church, with the other bishops as successors of the apostles. The Pope can teach infallibly only under strict conditions, when he defines a doctrine of faith or morals for the whole Church.

topics.title: The lay faithful
topics.summary: The Church teaches that all the baptized share in Christ’s priestly, prophetic and kingly mission, and that lay people are called to sanctify the world from within, through family, work and public life, as well as to take part in the Church’s own work.
